instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Meridian Dynamics is a boutique commercial property management firm specializing in smaller multi-unit portfolios. They manage 12 office buildings, focusing heavily on tenant retention and operational efficiency across their retail centers and logistics parks.
answers.pastInitiatives: We piloted a cloud-based project management tool last year to streamline tenant communications, but adoption was inconsistent because the implementation lacked clear ownership. We ultimately reverted to spreadsheets and email for most tracking, confirming that adopting new systems requires dedicated change management rather than just purchasing software.
answers.strategicGoals: The board has mandated that 25% of revenue should come from products or services that did not exist 3 years ago. This requires us to systematically explore adjacent markets, new customer segments, and alternative monetization models through strategic partnerships.
answers.additionalContext: Meridian Dynamics operates primarily through personal relationships and localized knowledge rather than large-scale standardized corporate frameworks.
answers.teamSize: The founder handles all product and technology decisions personally with occasional input from a part-time freelance developer. There is no formal engineering team — technical work is either done by the founder or outsourced to contractors on a project basis. Innovation bandwidth is essentially limited to whatever the founder can personally drive alongside day-to-day operations.

opportunities.title: IoT Energy Optimization Platform
opportunities.rationale: Implementing low-cost IoT sensors across the properties can provide granular data on energy consumption, allowing Meridian to offer highly personalized 'green management' packages to premium tenants.

first_actions: Identify one building for a pilot program measuring HVAC and lighting efficiency.
Source three low-cost sensor providers and define key metrics (kWh reduction).
Develop an internal 'Data Dashboard' template using existing spreadsheet skills.
resources_needed: Part-time consulting hours for initial integration setup.
Internal time commitment from the founder (approx. 10 hrs/week).
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve a 7% average reduction in energy costs in pilot buildings within 6 months.
milestones: Q1: Pilot installation and data collection complete.
Q2: Cost savings quantified and presented to leadership.

opportunities.title: Fractional Real Estate Investment Platform
opportunities.rationale: Given the low digital maturity and long time horizon, creating a fractional ownership platform allows Meridian to decouple revenue from pure management fees, potentially attracting outside capital and fulfilling the 25% diversification mandate.

first_actions: Conduct market research on existing fractional REITs in similar micro markets.
Define the legal structure for a tokenized or simplified investment vehicle.
Develop a basic white paper outlining ROI scenarios.
resources_needed: Contracted freelance developer specializing in fintech concepts.
Time allocation from leadership for long-term strategic planning.
execution_plan.success_metric: Launch the investment platform prototype and secure initial interest from 5 external investors within 12 months.
milestones: Q1: Completion of legal framework and white paper.
Q3: Beta launch of the fractional ownership model.

next_steps.action: Establish a formal, documented process for capturing customer feedback (even informal notes) and turning it into actionable product ideas.
Identify and assign ownership of the 'process documentation' task to mitigate the main barrier of process adoption.

key_weaknesses: Low digital maturity severely limits scalable operational efficiency and data utilization.
Informal innovation culture lacks standardized change management, leading to inconsistent project adoption (e.g., spreadsheet vs. tool).
High dependence on the founder for all technical decision-making creates a single point of failure regarding bandwidth and expertise.
Lack of formal customer feedback loop prevents proactive product/service diversification planning.
